questions.question: The sum of 11 numbers is 660. Find their average.
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

The **Average** of a set of numbers is the **Total Sum** divided by the **Count** of numbers.

Average = 660 ÷ 11

Average = 60

**∴ The correct answer is 60.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Sum of 11 numbers = 660

Total numbers (n) = 11

**Formula Used:**

Average = Sum of all observations ÷ Total number of observations

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/69f607e9483062c5e30ca44e86da16c8ec94b62dc79234d00e0e1432e5b77fb4.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Average = 660 ÷ 11

⇒ Average = 60

**∴ The correct answer is 60.**

**__Additional Information__**

Arithmetic Mean

The arithmetic mean (average) represents the central value of a finite set of numbers, calculated as the sum of all values divided by their count.

Finding the Sum

If the average and the total count are known, the total sum can be found using: Sum = Average × Total Count.

Effect of Operations

If every number in a set is increased, decreased, multiplied, or divided by a constant value **k**, the average also changes by that same constant **k**.</p

questions.question: Rs. 30000 is lent at compound interest (compounded annually) for 3 years. If the rate of interest is 10 percent for the first year, 20 percent for the second year and 30 percent for the third year, then what will be the total compound interest?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Principal = Rs.30,000

Rate for the first year = 10%

Rate for the second year = 20%

Rate for the third year = 30%

**Formula used:**

Amount (A) = P × {1 + (R/100)} T

Compound Interest (C.I) = (A - P)

Where, P = principal ; R = rate ; T = time

**Calculation:**

Amount (A) = P × {1 + (R/100)}T

⇒ 30000 × {1 + (10/100)} × {1 + (20/100)} × {1 + (30/100)}

 

⇒ 30000 × {1 + (1/10)} × {1 + (1/5)} × {1 + (3/10)}

 

⇒ 30000 × (11/10) × (6/5) × (13/10)

 

⇒ 60 × 11 × 6 × 13 = Rs.51480

 

Compound Interest (C.I) = (A - P)

 

⇒ (51480 - 30000) = Rs.21480

 

**∴ The correct answer is Rs.21480.**

questions.question: By selling 50 items, a shopkeeper gains the selling price of 10 items. What is his gain percent?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

When Profit = SP of x items, then CP (in terms of units) = Total items − x.

Profit = 10 units; Total items = 50 units.

⇒ CP = 50 − 10 = 40 units.

⇒ Gain % = (Profit ÷ CP) × 100 = (10 ÷ 40) × 100.

⇒ Gain % = 25%.

**∴ The correct answer is 25%.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Number of items sold = 50

Gain = Selling Price of 10 items

Gain = Total Selling Price (SP) − Total Cost Price (CP)

questions.question: Shopkeeper gave 30% discount on the article having marked price Rs. 3500. What will be the selling price of the article?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

If a 30% discount is applied on the article, the selling price becomes (100% − 30%) = 70% of its marked price.

Selling Price = 70% of 3500

Selling Price = (70 ÷ 100) × 3500

Selling Price = 2450

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 2450.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Marked Price (MP) = Rs. 3500

Discount percentage = 30%

**Formula Used:**

Discount Amount = MP × (Discount% ÷ 100)

Selling Price (SP) = MP − Discount Amount

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/53552b64e701833c85547a3db48e873dc375e72df6a70cc96f41f05ece3b6feb.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Discount Amount = 3500 × (30 ÷ 100)

⇒ Discount Amount = 3500 × 0.30

⇒ Discount Amount = 1050

⇒ SP = 3500 − 1050

⇒ SP = 2450

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 2450.**

**__Additional Information__**

Base of Calculations

Profit and Loss are always calculated on the Cost Price (CP), whereas the Discount is exclusively calculated on the Marked Price (MP).

Successive Discounts

The single equivalent discount for two successive discounts a% and b% can be calculated using the direct formula: Equivalent Discount = [a + b − (a × b) ÷ 100]%.

Marking Up Goods

When goods are marked up above the Cost Price to provide a discount but still achieve a certain profit: MP = CP × (100 + Profit%) ÷ (100 − Discount%).
